scenario: C10-ABLATION-01-NOTIFY-ON: wake-delivered + marker held at emit, CANONICAL DISCRIMINATOR ON
evidence: ablation.test.ts:NOTIFY-ON; consumeTerminal drives host.enqueueTerminalWake({kind:delivered}) -> markWakeDelivered(J); marker re-registered for SEAM A at emit; SEAM B holds lifecycle commit via perJobSuppressOriginatingCompletion (wasWakeDelivered=true)
load_bearing_invariant: C10 ON drops completion_result row from result.messages BEFORE appendAndEmit; framework barrier holds; ONE logical terminal event -> ZERO visible completion boxes from the originating turn

scenario: C10-ABLATION-01-NOTIFY-OFF: wake-delivered + marker held at emit, CANONICAL DISCRIMINATOR OFF
evidence: ablation.test.ts:NOTIFY-OFF; identical setup to NOTIFY-ON; framework_commits=0 (identical); completion_result rows=2 raw / 1 visible box
load_bearing_invariant: ISOLATION PROOF: framework_completion_commits is identical to NOTIFY-ON (both 0); the only difference is the message-layer filter outcome. SEAM A OFF leaks the originating turn's completion_result row even when SEAM B holds the lifecycle commit.

scenario: C10-ABLATION-01-NOTIFY-OFF-MULTI: TWO wakes delivered per-job, C10 OFF
evidence: ablation.test.ts:NOTIFY-OFF-MULTI; consumeTerminal for both J1 and J2; both wasWakeDelivered=true; SEAM B holds originating commit; completion_result row leaks through (per-job isolation lost)
load_bearing_invariant: Per-job narrow ownership correlation is load-bearing for multi-job isolation under wake-delivered SEAM B

scenario: C10-ABLATION-02-NON-NOTIFY: ordinary completion (no notify marker), C10 OFF
evidence: ablation.test.ts:NON-NOTIFY; SEAM A off and no owned jobs -> nothing to filter; SEAM B ALLOWs (no markers)
load_bearing_invariant: No regression for ordinary completion path

scenario: C10-ABLATION-03-LOST-WAKE: dispatch FAILED case, C10 OFF
evidence: ablation.test.ts:LOST-WAKE; consumeTerminal with host outcome=rejected -> markWakeDispatchFailed; SEAM B ALLOWs (wasWakeDispatchFailed), completion commits; row leaks through with C10 off
load_bearing_invariant: Lost-wake ALLOW branch unaffected by C10 ablation

scenario: C10-ABLATION-04-FAST-EXIT: marker consumed via resolveObligation, no wake
evidence: ablation.test.ts:FAST-EXIT; resolveObligation drains marker without wake; SEAM B ALLOWs

scenario: C10-ABLATION-05-MULTI-JOB-ON: J20 consumed, J40 still alive, C10 ON
evidence: ablation.test.ts:MULTI-JOB-ON; narrow per-job filter suppresses only owned-and-outstanding (J40 only)
load_bearing_invariant: Per-job ownership-aware filter still protects when C10 is ON

scenario: C10-ABLATION-05-MULTI-JOB-OFF: J20 consumed, J40 still alive, C10 OFF
evidence: ablation.test.ts:MULTI-JOB-OFF; per-job isolation lost; completion_result row leaks; SEAM B holds because J20+J40 both alive
load_bearing_invariant: Per-job isolation is part of what C10 protects
